title: Port books missed $12.3 million in depreciation and carried $3.2 million in retired assets

beats.text: Port streets and other land improvements had been treated as permanent.

visual.sub: Previously undepreciated improvements required a $12.3 million adjustment

beats.text: The Port determined those improvements wore out and should have depreciated.

visual.heading: How the Port classified the assets

beats.text: It raised opening accumulated depreciation by $12.3 million.
A second adjustment removed $3.2 million in improvements no longer in service.

visual.kicker: A separate $3.2 million adjustment removed retired assets

beats.text: The audited City accounts record both changes.
Auditors also found asset descriptions too incomplete to identify some property.

visual.kicker: A separate $3.2 million adjustment removed retired assets

beats.text: They recommended inventory records listing locations, costs and useful lives.

visual.kicker: A separate $3.2 million adjustment removed retired assets

beats.text: The Port proposed counting in phases because a comprehensive count required more resources.

visual.kicker: The Port proposed verifying assets in phases

beats.text: Land and land improvements would come first.

visual.kicker: The Port proposed verifying assets in phases

beats.text: In 2011 it said the last property cycle had ended in 2004.

visual.kicker: The Port proposed verifying assets in phases

beats.text: The records confirm the accounting entries. Completion of the inventory remains undocumented.
Every source is linked in the case file below.
